# Teaching {.page-heading}
During my PhD at the University of Utah, I was the instructor of record for seven undergraduate mathematics courses and a teaching assistant for two additional courses. My students came from a wide range of academic backgrounds, including mathematics, engineering, computer science, and other STEM disciplines.

### Instructor of Record

**MATH 2270 — Linear Algebra**  
Summer 2026 · Fall 2025 · Summer 2025

**MATH 2250 — Differential Equations and Linear Algebra**  
Spring 2026 · Spring 2025 

**MATH 3140 — Vector Calculus and Partial Differential Equations for Engineers**  
Fall 2024 · Fall 2023

# Mentorship

### Summer Graduate School Preview Program
**Undergraduate Research Mentor · Summers 2022 & 2023**  
Through the weeklong Graduate School Preview program, I mentored undergraduate teams on mathematical biology projects exploring Peto’s paradox and how phenotypic switching helps microbial communities survive antibiotic treatment. I guided students through project design, background research, mathematical analysis, computation, and presentation of their results.

### High School Mathematical Modeling Workshop
**High School Mathematical Modeling Mentor · Fall 2022**  
I helped run a semester-long after-school workshop at the University of Utah for high school students interested in mathematical modeling competitions such as [HiMCM](https://www.comap.com/contests/himcm-midmcm) and the [M3 Challenge](https://m3challenge.siam.org/). Students learned to develop and analyze models using difference and differential equations and statistical methods, implement them in Python and MATLAB, and communicate their results through technical reports.
